subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should ordinary external plugins be allowed to invoke plugin-registered Gateway methods, and under what authorization and exposure model beyond the current bundled/trusted-official-only path?
rationale: The remaining work changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose raw dispatch, curated capabilities, trusted-only access, or no third-party access.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
options.body: Expose only approved Gateway methods or typed plugin capabilities with caller attribution, explicit trust/allowlist policy, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-only access
options.body: Treat the current main implementation as the intended boundary and require external plugins to use another documented seam or trusted-official distribution.

options.title: Allow broad raw dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller to more plugins, accepting the broader security and compatibility surface as an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved Gateway methods or typed plugin capabilities with caller attribution, explicit trust/allowlist policy, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the current trusted-only Gateway runtime path and has the strongest recent history around this Gateway/Plugin SDK security boundary.
